scenes.headline: The Log Book, for agents
scenes.sub: Log it, in by noon, catch the bag
scenes.line: This is the new Log Book, as an agent sees it. Log your documents, hand them in by noon, and catch the bag.

scenes.headline: Your number, your password
scenes.line: Open Ricky Rampersad branch dot com, slash log book. Sign in with your agent number, and the password you use for the fact find.

scenes.headline: In by twelve noon, down at one
scenes.line: There is one bag a day. It goes down at the one o'clock bag exchange. Papers in the branch's hands by twelve noon go on it. After twelve, they wait for the next day's bag.

scenes.headline: It knows where it goes
scenes.line: Choose the document first. The Log Book routes it to the right department, from the branch's own history, and says how sure it is.

scenes.headline: Only your clients
scenes.line: Then find the client. Type a name, an e-mail, or a policy number. You only ever see your own clients. Tick the policy the papers are for.

scenes.headline: What usually comes with it
scenes.line: If something usually travels with it, the Log Book asks. A surrender usually comes with proof of I D. One tap adds it.

scenes.headline: It tells you if it catches the bag
scenes.line: Confirm the papers are complete and signed, and press Log it. You get a reference, and the Log Book tells you if it will catch today's bag.

scenes.headline: The rush comes just too late
scenes.line: Here is why it matters. In the old book, fifty seven in every hundred papers came in after twelve, and waited a day. More came in between twelve and one than in any hour of the morning, just after the bag closes.

scenes.headline: One hour to catch it
scenes.line: At eleven, if you logged papers and have not handed them in, the Log Book e-mails you. One hour to catch today's bag.

scenes.headline: Every step, on your phone
scenes.line: My log shows every step. Logged. Received by the branch. On the bag. And confirmed by the department.

scenes.headline: In by twelve

rows.b: In by 12 noon, on the 1 pm bag
rows.i: Stamped when you log, when the branch receives, when it goes

rows.b: Missed the bag? The branch is asked why
rows.i: And you are copied on the e-mail

rows.b: A contract to deliver: twenty days
rows.i: Chased at day fifteen and day eighteen

scenes.line: The rule is simple. In by twelve, on the one o'clock bag. If it misses the bag, the branch is asked why, and you are copied. A contract you collect to deliver has twenty days.

scenes.headline: Your whole team
scenes.line: Unit managers, like Akaash, see their whole team under My team. Every agent's papers, or one agent at a time. Nobody sees another unit.
Log it. In by noon. Catch the bag.
